title: 'ADS Created'
description: |
    This event logs when a named file stream (Alternate Data Stream) is created, 
    and it generates events that log the hash of the contents of the file to which the stream is assigned (the unnamed stream),
    as well as the contents of the named stream. 
    There are malware variants that drop their executables or configuration settings via browser downloads, 
    and this event is aimed at capturing that based on the browser attaching a Zone.Identifier "mark of the web" stream.

title: 'Proc Access (Sysmon Alert)'
description: |
    The process accessed event reports when a process opens another process, an operation that is often followed by information queries or reading and writing the address space of the target process. 
    This enables detection of hacking tools that read the memory contents of processes like Local Security Authority (Lsass.exe) in order to steal credentials for use in Pass-the-Hash attacks. 
    Enabling it can generate significant amounts of logging if there are diagnostic utilities active that repeatedly open processes to query their state, so it generally should only be done so with filters that remove expected accesses.

title: 'DLL Loaded (Noisy)'
description: |
    The Image Loaded event logs when a module (usually DLL) is loaded in a specific process.
    This event is disabled by default and needs to be configured with the –l option.
    It indicates the process in which the module is loaded, hashes and signature information.
    The signature is created asynchronously for performance reasons and indicates if the file was removed after loading.
    This event should be configured carefully, as monitoring all image load events will generate a large number of events.
    Marked as noisy due to many events.

author: Zach Mathis

title: 'Proc Injection'
description: |
    The CreateRemoteThread (Process Injection) event detects when a process creates a thread in another process. 
    This technique is used by malware to inject code and hide in other processes. 
    The event indicates the source and target process. 
    It gives information on the code that will be run in the new thread: StartAddress, StartModule and StartFunction. 
    Note that StartModule and StartFunction fields are inferred, they might be empty if the starting address is outside loaded modules or known exported functions.

title: 'Proc Injection (Sysmon Alert)'
description: |
    The CreateRemoteThread (Process Injection) event detects when a process creates a thread in another process. 
    This technique is used by malware to inject code and hide in other processes. 
    The event indicates the source and target process. 
    It gives information on the code that will be run in the new thread: StartAddress, StartModule and StartFunction. 
    Note that StartModule and StartFunction fields are inferred, they might be empty if the starting address is outside loaded modules or known exported functions.

title: 'Clipboard Change (Sysmon Alert)'
description: |
    The main DFIR purpose is to capture files that attackers copy over via RDP, attacker commands that were copied and pasted, etc...
    This event is generated when the system clipboard contents change.
    Passwords and other sensitive information may be leaked when copied into the clipboard so heavy filtering to prevent this is necessary.
    The copied contents are not saved in the event log but archived to the same protected folder as the File Delete event does. (C:\Sysmon)
    SYSTEM privileges are required to access this folder. 
    Hashes of the files can also be saved.
    Session is where the process writing to clipboard is running: System(0), Interactive, Remote, etc...
    ClientInfo will store originating hostname and IP address in the case of a remote session. (i.e. Attacker using RDP.)

    and it generates events that log the hash of the contents of the file to which the stream is assigned (the unnamed stream),

    FilterGoogleUpdate:

db1fa879-6d12-4bd1-b947-ee5dc565c55e.raw:
author: Defa Mulya Pratama
date: 2026-10-08

title: 'Susp CmdLine (Possible Inhibit System Recovery)'
description: |
    Detects commands commonly used by ransomware and destructive malware to inhibit system recovery, such as deleting or resizing Volume Shadow Copies, deleting backup catalogs, or disabling Windows automatic recovery.
    This is the Sysmon process creation (EventID 1) version of the Security 4688 rule.

id: db1fa879-6d12-4bd1-b947-ee5dc565c55e
level: high
status: test
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: sysmon
detection:
    selection_base:
        Channel: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational
        EventID: 1
    selection_cmd_vssadmin_delete:
        Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'delete'
            - 'shadows'
    selection_cmd_vssadmin_resize:
        Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'resize'
            - 'shadowstorage'
    selection_cmd_wmic_shadow:
        Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'shadowcopy'
            - 'delete'
    selection_cmd_wbadmin:
        Image|endswith: '\wbadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'delete'
            - 'catalog'
    selection_cmd_bcdedit:
        Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'recoveryenabled no'
            - 'recoveryenabled off'
            - 'ignoreallfailures'
    condition: selection_base and 1 of selection_cmd_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative maintenance of shadow copies or backups, which is uncommon and should be verified.
tags:
    - attack.impact
    - attack.t1490
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
    - https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/its-all-fun-and-games-until-ransomware-deletes-the-shadow-copies/

title: 'Proc Access'
description: |
    The process accessed event reports when a process opens another process, an operation that is often followed by information queries or reading and writing the address space of the target process. 
    This enables detection of hacking tools that read the memory contents of processes like Local Security Authority (Lsass.exe) in order to steal credentials for use in Pass-the-Hash attacks. 
    Enabling it can generate significant amounts of logging if there are diagnostic utilities active that repeatedly open processes to query their state, so it generally should only be done so with filters that remove expected accesses.
    Source User and Target User are not available in earlier versions of Sysmon.

id: 39503291-25e2-4d79-86d4-fb18804c5f21
level: low  # Marked as low due to a high possisbility of false positives.
status: test
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: sysmon
    definition: 'SrcUser and TgtUser fields are not be present in older versions of Sysmon.'
detection:
    selection_basic:
        Channel: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational
        EventID: 10
    selection_no_alerts:
        - RuleName: ''
        - RuleName: '-'
    filter_allowlist:
        - SourceImage: 'C:\Program Files (x86)\McAfee\VirusScan Enterprise\VsTskMgr.exe'
        - SourceImage: 'C:\Program Files\Common Files\McAfee\SystemCore\mcshield.exe'
        - SourceImage: 'C:\Program Files\VMware\VMware Tools\vmtoolsd.exe'
        - SourceImage: 'C:\windows\system32\MRT.exe'
    filter_lsass_to_winlogon:
        SourceImage: 'C:\Windows\system32\lsass.exe'
        TargetImage: 'C:\windows\system32\winlogon.exe'
    condition: selection_basic and selection_no_alerts and not filter_allowlist and not filter_lsass_to_winlogon
falsepositives:
tags:
    - sysmon
references:
    - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon

title: 'Proc Tampering'
description: |
    Detects process hollowing or process herpaderping techniques which would normally not be visible in Task Manager.
    Process hollowing is when malware launches a legitimate process in a suspended state and replaces legitimate code in the process with malicious code. 
    This malicious code is then executed by the process, with whatever permissions are assigned to the process.
    Process herpaderping is where malware modifies its image on the disk to look like legitimate software after the malware is loaded. 
    When security software scans the on-disk file, it will see a harmless file while the malicious code runs in memory.

    The Change File Creation Time Event is registered when a file creation time is explicitly modified by a process.

db13c364-2254-4247-8c53-da1a7c4bdb78.raw:
author: Defa Mulya Pratama
date: 2026-10-07

title: 'Susp CmdLine (Possible Inhibit System Recovery)'
description: |
    Detects commands commonly used by ransomware and destructive malware to inhibit system recovery, such as deleting or resizing Volume Shadow Copies, deleting backup catalogs, or disabling Windows automatic recovery.
    This rule uses the built-in Windows Security "Process Creation" event (4688) so that it works without Sysmon. Command line auditing must be enabled.

id: db13c364-2254-4247-8c53-da1a7c4bdb78
level: high
status: test
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
    description: Process Creation with command line option logging needs to be turned on.
detection:
    selection_base:
        Channel: Security
        EventID: 4688
    selection_cmd_vssadmin_delete:
        NewProcessName|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'delete'
            - 'shadows'
    selection_cmd_vssadmin_resize:
        NewProcessName|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'resize'
            - 'shadowstorage'
    selection_cmd_wmic_shadow:
        NewProcessName|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'shadowcopy'
            - 'delete'
    selection_cmd_wbadmin:
        NewProcessName|endswith: '\wbadmin.exe'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'delete'
            - 'catalog'
    selection_cmd_bcdedit:
        NewProcessName|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'recoveryenabled no'
            - 'recoveryenabled off'
            - 'ignoreallfailures'
    condition: selection_base and 1 of selection_cmd_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative maintenance of shadow copies or backups, which is uncommon and should be verified.
tags:
    - attack.impact
    - attack.t1490
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
    - https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/its-all-fun-and-games-until-ransomware-deletes-the-shadow-copies/
sample-evtx: |
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <Event xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event">
      <System>
        <Provider Name="Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing" Guid="{54849625-5478-4994-A5BA-3E3B0328C30D}"/>
        <EventID>4688</EventID>
        <Version>2</Version>
        <Level>0</Level>
        <Task>13312</Task>
        <Opcode>0</Opcode>
        <Keywords>0x8020000000000000</Keywords>
        <TimeCreated SystemTime="2026-10-08T03:21:07.159387500Z"/>
        <EventRecordID>284512</EventRecordID>
        <Correlation/>
        <Execution ProcessID="4" ThreadID="6292"/>
        <Channel>Security</Channel>
        <Computer>wef.windomain.local</Computer>
        <Security/>
      </System>
      <EventData>
        <Data Name="SubjectUserSid">S-1-5-18</Data>
        <Data Name="SubjectUserName">WEF$</Data>
        <Data Name="SubjectDomainName">WINDOMAIN</Data>
        <Data Name="SubjectLogonId">0x3e7</Data>
        <Data Name="NewProcessId">0x1a40</Data>
        <Data Name="NewProcessName">C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe</Data>
        <Data Name="TokenElevationType">%%1936</Data>
        <Data Name="ProcessId">0x24c</Data>
        <Data Name="CommandLine">vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet</Data>
        <Data Name="TargetUserSid">S-1-0-0</Data>
        <Data Name="TargetUserName">-</Data>
        <Data Name="TargetDomainName">-</Data>
        <Data Name="TargetLogonId">0x0</Data>
        <Data Name="ParentProcessName">C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe</Data>
        <Data Name="MandatoryLabel">S-1-16-16384</Data>

title: 'Logon Proc Registered With LSA'
description: 'A logon process has registered with the Local Security Authority (LSA). Logon requests will now be accepted from this source. Technically, the event does not come from the registration of a trusted logon process, but from a confirmation that the process is a trusted logon process. If it is a trusted logon process, the event generates. A logon process is a trusted part of the OS that handles logon methods (network, interactive, etc.)'

    condition: selection
falsepositives:

5b6e58ee-c231-4a54-9eee-af2577802e08.raw:
author: Zach Mathis
date: 2020-11-08
modified: 2025-02-10

title: 'Process Ran With High Privilege'
description: |
    Malware may generate a 4673 event (A privileged service was called) when dumping hashes or wiping disk. 
    For example, mimikatz will generate 4 logs using SeTcbPrivilege (Act as part of the OS.) 
    Disk wipers like bcwipe will also generate this.
    More legitimate filepaths may have to be added to the filter.
    This is marked as a medium alert as there is a high possibility for false positives.

id: 5b6e58ee-c231-4a54-9eee-af2577802e08
level: medium
status: stable
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection:
        Channel: Security
        EventID: 4673
    filter: 
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\net.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\audiodg.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\mmc.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\net.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\explorer.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\SettingSyncHost.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\sdiagnhost.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\dwm.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\WinSAT.exe'
        - ProcessName|endswith: 'ngentask.exe'
        - ProcessName: 'C:\Windows\System32\taskhostw.exe'
        - ProcessName|startswith: 'C:\Program Files'
        - SubjectUserName: 'LOCAL SERVICE'
    condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
    - normal system usage
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.t1561
    - attack.impact
references:
    - https://www.ultimatewindowssecurity.com/securitylog/encyclopedia/event.aspx?eventID=4673
    - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4673
sample-evtx: ./sample-evtx/DeepBlueCLI/mimikatz-privesc-hashdump.evtx
ruletype: Hayabusa
5b6e58ee-c231-4a54-9eee-af2577802e08.desc:
Malware may generate a 4673 event (A privileged service was called) when dumping hashes or wiping disk.
For example, mimikatz will generate 4 logs using SeTcbPrivilege (Act as part of the OS.)
Disk wipers like bcwipe will also generate this.
More legitimate filepaths may have to be added to the filter.
This is marked as a medium alert as there is a high possibility for false positives.

a5b3ebf0-141a-4264-b2ff-400c0d515fca.raw:
author: Zach Mathis
date: 2023-06-08
modified: 2025-02-10

title: Explicit Logon Attempt (Noisy)
description: |
    (From ultimatewindowsecurity.com)
    This log is generated when
    1. A user connects to a server or runs a program locally using alternate credentials.
       For instance a user maps a drive to a server but specifies a different user's credentials or opens a shortcut under RunAs by shift-control-right-clicking on the shortcut,
       selecting Run as..., and then filling in a different user's credentials in the dialog box that appears.  Or a user logs on to a web site using new specific credentials.
    2. When a process logs on as a different account such as when the Scheduled Tasks service starts a task as the specified user.
    3. With User Account Control enabled, an end user runs a program requiring admin authority.  You will get this event where the process information is consent.exe.
       Unfortunately the Subject does not identify the end user.
    4. Logging on interactively to a server with a domain account. (Two 4624 events will also be generated.)
    This logon event is unique in that it is logged on the source computer and not the target computer like most other logon events.
    Also, it will be logged regardless of the logon being successful or not so consider it an attempt and not necessarily an actual successful logon.

id: a5b3ebf0-141a-4264-b2ff-400c0d515fca
level: informational
status: stable
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection_basic:
        Channel: Security
        EventID: 4648
    selection_system_noise_1:
        - TargetUserName|endswith: '$'
        - SubjectUserName|endswith: '$'
    selection_system_noise_2:
        TargetUserName|re: '(DWM|UMFD)-([0-9]|1[0-3])$' #Filter out default Desktop Windows Manager and User Mode Driver Framework accounts
        IpAddress: '-'
    filter_SuspiciousProcess:
        - ProcessName|endswith: 'powershell.exe'
        - ProcessName|endswith: 'WMIC.exe'
    condition: selection_basic and not filter_SuspiciousProcess and 1 of selection_system_noise*
falsepositives:
    - normal system usage
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.lateral-movement
references:
    - https://www.ultimatewindowssecurity.com/securitylog/encyclopedia/event.aspx?eventID=4648
ruletype: Hayabusa

sample-message: |
    A logon was attempted using explicit credentials.

    Subject:
        Security ID:		SYSTEM
        Account Name:		SEC504STUDENT$
        Account Domain:		SEC504
        Logon ID:		0x3E7
        Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}

    Account Whose Credentials Were Used:
        Account Name:		Sec504
        Account Domain:		SEC504STUDENT
        Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}

    Target Server:
        Target Server Name:	localhost
        Additional Information:	localhost

    Process Information:
        Process ID:		0x514
        Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe

    Network Information:
        Network Address:	127.0.0.1
        Port:			0

    This event is generated when a process attempts to log on an account by explicitly specifying that accounts credentials.  This most commonly occurs in batch-type configurations such as scheduled tasks, or when using the RUNAS command.

9e8b6cdb-9991-488b-a7b3-2eec7aa64679.raw:
author: Zach Mathis
date: 2022-04-18
modified: 2022-12-16

title: NewInteractive Logon (Suspicious Process)
description: Tries to detect token impersonation by tools like Cobalt Strike.

id: 9e8b6cdb-9991-488b-a7b3-2eec7aa64679
level: medium
status: stable
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection_basic:
        Channel: Security
        EventID: 4624       # Logon Succesful
        LogonType: 9
    filter_ProcessAllowlist:  # This should usually be svchost.exe. Add more to the list below if you have any false positives.
        ProcessName:
            - 'C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe'
    condition: selection_basic and not filter_ProcessAllowlist
falsepositives:
    - uncommon tools used for admin
tags:
references:
    - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=borfuQGrB8g (Cobalt Strike Threat Hunting - Chad Tilbury)
ruletype: Hayabusa

sample-message: |
    An account was successfully logged on.

    Subject:
        Security ID:		S-1-5-21-3445421715-2530690580-3149308974-1193
        Account Name:		user
        Account Domain:		domain
        Logon ID:		0x6ABE62

    Logon Information:
        Logon Type:		9
        Restricted Admin Mode:	-
        Virtual Account:		No
        Elevated Token:		Yes

    Impersonation Level:		Impersonation

    New Logon:
        Security ID:		S-1-5-21-3445421715-2530690580-3149308974-1193
        Account Name:		user
        Account Domain:		domain
        Logon ID:		0xD7F582C
        Linked Logon ID:		0x0
        Network Account Name:	user
        Network Account Domain:	domain.lan
        Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}

    Process Information:
        Process ID:		0x2044
        Process Name:		C:\Windows\Temp\temp.exe

    Network Information:
        Workstation Name:	-
        Source Network Address:	-
        Source Port:		-

    Detailed Authentication Information:
        Logon Process:		Advapi  
        Authentication Package:	Negotiate
        Transited Services:	-
        Package Name (NTLM only):	-
        Key Length:		0

    This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.

    The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.

    The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).

    The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.

    The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.

8c1899fe-493d-4faf-aae1-0853a33a3278.raw:
author: Zach Mathis
date: 2021-12-17
modified: 2025-02-10

title: Explicit Logon Attempt
description: |
    (From ultimatewindowsecurity.com)
    This log is generated when
    1. A user connects to a server or runs a program locally using alternate credentials.
       For instance a user maps a drive to a server but specifies a different user's credentials or opens a shortcut under RunAs by shift-control-right-clicking on the shortcut,
       selecting Run as..., and then filling in a different user's credentials in the dialog box that appears.  Or a user logs on to a web site using new specific credentials.
    2. When a process logs on as a different account such as when the Scheduled Tasks service starts a task as the specified user.
    3. With User Account Control enabled, an end user runs a program requiring admin authority.  You will get this event where the process information is consent.exe.
       Unfortunately the Subject does not identify the end user.
    4. Logging on interactively to a server with a domain account. (Two 4624 events will also be generated.)
    This logon event is unique in that it is logged on the source computer and not the target computer like most other logon events.
    Also, it will be logged regardless of the logon being successful or not so consider it an attempt and not necessarily an actual successful logon.

id: 8c1899fe-493d-4faf-aae1-0853a33a3278
level: informational
status: stable
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
detection:
    selection_basic:
        Channel: Security
        EventID: 4648
    filter_ComputerAccounts:
        - TargetUserName|endswith: '$'
        - SubjectUserName|endswith: '$'
    filter_SystemAccounts:
        TargetUserName|re: '(DWM|UMFD)-([0-9]|1[0-3])$' #Filter out default Desktop Windows Manager and User Mode Driver Framework accounts
        IpAddress: '-'                                  #Don't filter if the IP address is remote to catch attackers who created backdoor accounts that look like DWM-12, etc..
    filter_SuspiciousProcess:
        - ProcessName|endswith: 'powershell.exe'
        - ProcessName|endswith: 'WMIC.exe'
    condition: selection_basic and not 1 of filter*
falsepositives:
    - normal system usage
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.lateral-movement
references:
    - https://www.ultimatewindowssecurity.com/securitylog/encyclopedia/event.aspx?eventID=4648
ruletype: Hayabusa

sample-message: |
    A logon was attempted using explicit credentials.

    Subject:
        Security ID:		S-1-5-21-2977773840-2930198165-1551093962-1000
        Account Name:		SEC504STUDENT
        Account Domain:		SEC504
        Logon ID:		0x3E7
        Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}

    Account Whose Credentials Were Used:
        Account Name:		Sec504
        Account Domain:		SEC504STUDENT
        Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}

    Target Server:

    Process Information:
        Process ID:		0x514
        Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe

    Network Information:
        Network Address:	127.0.0.1
        Port:			0

    This event is generated when a process attempts to log on an account by explicitly specifying that accounts credentials.  This most commonly occurs in batch-type configurations such as scheduled tasks, or when using the RUNAS command.

title: RDP Logon
details: 'TgtUser: %UserDataUser% ¦ SessID: %UserDataSessionID% ¦ SrcIP: %UserDataAddress%'
description: |
    This event is created when a new local session is created for either a local or remote interactive login when a user successfully authenticates and there is no existing local session.
    This event will be created when a user logs on for the first time or after a logout but not after just a disconnect because the session will still exist.
    In that case, a reconnect event will be created.
    The Local Session Manager is responsible for creating or finding existing local sessions to support interactive logins.
    Note that local sessions are different from logon sessions.
    Local sessions represent the logon sessions, desktop layout, processes, etc. associated with an interactive logon. 
    SrcIP will be an IP address if it is a remote session and "LOCAL" if it is a local session.
    This event gives the same information in Remote Connection Manager 1149, Local Session Manager 22 and Security 4648.

title: 'RDP Conn (Noisy)'
details: ''
description: |
    This event is generated when anyone connects to RDP and sends data. It does not need to be a legitimate RDP connection.
    Unfortunately, there are no details about the remote machine.
    This event is noisy and will generate a lot of logs and is of limited investigative value.
    If you see a large number of these events, but not successful logon events with EID 1149, etc... then it may indicate a brute force attack.
    The Security event log will have more information so this event is only useful if the Security event logs are not available.

    Uses RDP so I am refering to these as RDP Logons as that is what most people will expect.
    On newer OSes (Win 7+, 2012+), this event is logged only when a user successfully logs on to a RDP session.
    On older OSes (Vista, 2008), this event is logged when a user logs on to a RDP session, regardless of success.
    This event might be be created when rdesktop is used as a client and NLA is disabled.

title: Computer Startup
details: 'MajorVer: %Data[1]% ¦ BuildNum: %Data[2]%'
description: |
    The computer started up. This event is important because it also contains the OS version information.
    %Data[3]% contains the Service Pack name (Ex: Service Pack 1) for Windows 7 systems but can be infered from the build number so is left out.
    %Data[4]% contains processor license information (Ex: Multiprocessor Free) but is not so useful so is left out.
    %Data[5]% contains the Revision (a.k.a. Update Version) Number in Windows 7 logs.
    Windows 10+ seems to always output 0 for this so it is not a reliable source for identifying the Revision Number.

description: Malware will often create services for persistence and use BASE64 encoded strings to execute malicious code or abuse legitimate binaries like cmd.exe, powershell, etc... inside the path to execute. Normally, services will not run built-in binaries, run from user or temp folders or contain encoded data.
id: dbbfd9f3-9508-478b-887e-03ddb9236909
level: high
status: test
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: system
detection:
    selection:
        Channel: System
        EventID: 7045
    selection_SuspiciousPathNames:
        - ImagePath|re: '[a-zA-Z0-9\/+=]{50}' # Looks for 50 characters or more of base64 encoded strings
        - ImagePath|contains: 'powershell'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'cmd.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'csc.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'mshta.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'regsvr32.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'rundll32.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'wscript.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'cscript.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'msiexec.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'certutil.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'bitsadmin.exe'
        - ImagePath|contains: 'appdata'
        - ImagePath|contains: '%SYSTEMROOT%'
    condition: selection and selection_SuspiciousPathNames
falsepositives:
    - Some legitimate drivers
    - Zoom Sharing Service
    - Epson Printer Drivers
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1543.003
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
ruletype: Hayabusa

Normally, services will not run built-in binaries, run from user or temp folders or contain encoded data.

082fbbf5-bb05-468c-ad9c-ef2a383bb293.raw:
author: Zach Mathis

title: 'BSOD'
details: 'ErrorCodes: %param1% ¦ MemoryDump: %param2%'
description: |
    Blue Screen Of Death. MS calls these Bug Check Errors.
    param1 will contain various error codes for debugging:
    example: 0x0000009f (0x0000000000000003, 0xffffe682fdfaf570, 0xfffff800666c4750, 0xffffe6831844f050)
        - 0x0000009f is the Bug Check Code (a.k.a. Stop Code) meaning DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
        - 0x0000000000000003 indicates the type of inconsistency. In this case, 0x3 means the system is transitioning from a sleep state (S4 or S5) to an awake state (S0).
        - 0xffffe682fdfaf570 is a pointer to the DEVICE_OBJECT structure representing the device that is being enumerated.
        - 0xfffff800666c4750 is a pointer to the IRP (I/O Request Packet) that was pending for the device object.
        - 0xffffe6831844f050 is a pointer to the NTSTATUS code indicating the cause of the failure.
    param2 is the path to a memory dump (ex: C:\WINDOWS\MEMORY.DMP)
    param3 is the report ID (ex: cf65ecb3-8a81-4a04-89ae-8d1fff1aecf8)

id: 082fbbf5-bb05-468c-ad9c-ef2a383bb293
level: medium
status: test
logsource:

    service: system
detection:
    selection:
        Channel: 'System'
        ProviderName: Microsoft-Windows-WER-SystemErrorReporting

    condition: selection
falsepositives:
tags:
references:
ruletype: Hayabusa
